newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA revises guidelines on Australia bank risk.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA revises guidelines on Australia bank risk.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia said Wednesday it had released new prudential supervision guidelines on capital adequacy for commercial banks' market risks.

The guidelines, which come into effect at the end of 1997, are Australia's response to the international guidelines issued by the Basle Committee on Banking Supervision in January 1996, the RBA said in a statement.

The impact of the new requirements would vary from bank to bank but it was not expected that the Australian banking system as a whole would need to raise significant additional capital top meet the guidelines.
The new guidelines, contained in Prudential Statement C3, addressed the risks for banks arising from fluctuations in interest rates, exchange rates, equity prices and commodity prices, the RBA said.
Banks would have a choice between two broad approaches in calculating their market risk exposure, one based on a standard supervisory model or one based on banks' own internal models.

Banks could use their own model as long as the underlying parameters met various minimum standards and the broader risk management practices surrounding the use of such models were satisfactory, the RBA said.
The RBA said it would be working this year with those banks wishing to use internal models to satisfy itself that their models met the conditions.

The decision to allow internal models reflected the progress banks had made in measuring and managing their risk exposure over the past decade and aimed to encourage banks to improve further their risk management systems, the RBA said.
